content.text: The text discusses tabes mesenterica, or tuberculosis of the mesenteric glands. Symptoms may include leg cramps from nerve pressure, oedema and dilated abdominal veins from venous compression, ascites, abdominal tumors, emaciation, fever, chronic diarrhoea, and greasy, pale stools caused by intestinal and glandular disease. Diagnosis relies on a hard, irregular, nodular umbilical mass while excluding fecal, omental, and cancerous tumors. Prognosis is highly unfavorable, with recovery rarely documented; possible improvement may occur only when disease is localized and glands undergo calcification or absorption before extensive caseation obstructs chyle flow. Pulmonary tuberculosis, intestinal ulceration, extensive gland involvement, rickets, and poor nutrition accelerate progression. Treatment is mainly preventive and palliative: control scrofulous, respiratory, and gastrointestinal disease; maintain hygiene, digestion, and nutrition; regulate diet; relieve pain and diarrhoea; and use tonics, iron, phosphates, cod-liver oil, and occasionally pancreatized foods. The remainder is an extensive alphabetical index of diseases, symptoms, anatomy, treatments, and page references.
